name: Pete's Point
text: [overview] A simple snow couloir on Pete's Point's north face, mostly a side trip when hiking in the Wallowas.
[detailed_rack] For a roped ascent, add a couple of screws and pickets.
[what_to_bring] ice axe.
[what_to_bring] crampons — ice may be present
[approach] Pete's Point sits above the lake between Tenderfoot Pass and Polaris Pass, and the route is the snow couloir on its north face.
[approach] Carry an ice axe for the couloir;

name: Full Richardson
text: [overview] Up a distinct couloir on the North Face: two WI2/3 steps and about 300 ft of moderate snow lead to the 30m crux, steep aerated ice with poor gear but great axe sticks, behaving more like alpine than water ice.
[overview] A picket above the curtain makes the belay;
[overview] Moderate snow in the bowl follows, around 600 feet to the summit;
[overview] Snow steepens under the summit block and may be loose at the very top;
[detailed_rack] Screws (with stubbies) and pickets.
[approach] Two short steps of ice or snow, depending on the season, come first, then moderate snow leads up the couloir.
[approach] Watch the snow stability here and check the avalanche forecast.

name: Nine O'clock Gully
text: [overview] It needs deep snow to be in shape and might carry a cornice.
[descent_text] Either gully needs solid snow cover to be in condition, and a cornice may cap the top of this one, so look it over from below before committing.

name: West Rib
text: [overview] The lower ridge is moderate snow;
[overview] Protection is rarely needed until the pinnacle, so most parties carry a few pickets or screws for the snow and a light rack of nuts and slings for the top.

name: Southwest Ridge
text: [overview] Easiest access when snow closes the Summit Lake road, and a handy way in for skiers after the bowls beneath the top.
[watch_out] In mid-May the forest between about 6,000 and 7,000 ft is confusing, and a snowshoe track there can melt out..
[watch_out] In mid-May the snow on the final summit ridge swings between firm and postholing;
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — may be needed
[approach] In mid-May snow can still cover the forest road from about 4,900 ft, adding road miles on snowshoes, while the first mile of trail is often already bare.
[seasonal_guidance] By late May the snow is consolidated from about 6,000 ft to the top, crampons are optional, and a glissade drops roughly 1,500 ft from the summit..
[pro_tips] In late April an early start finds snow firm enough to climb in boots, with crampons needed only for the upper third.

name: Black Spider - Fric-Amos
text: [overview] On Hood's east face, the Black Spider wall's left flank has 3 ice and mixed pitches, with snowfields and gullies between them.
[overview] P2, the key pitch: a full 60m of it from the snowfield's upper left corner.
[overview] Snow gully above, toward the rock band upper right.
[overview] P3: a brief ice step right of the band onto upper snow;
[approach] From Timberline, follow the South Side approach, then cross the White River Glacier and continue around to the foot of the wall.
[approach] The route starts on the left side of the wall, after crossing the bergschrund at the head of the Newton Clark Glacier.

name: Black Spider - Three Little Monkeys (Burkhardt-Getlin)
text: [overview] Six pitches, with steep snow on P6 up to the ridge of the summit.
[overview] the party instead went right, across loose, steep snow, to a chimney of vertical mud that stands out.
[detailed_rack] Pins, Specters, pickets, cams and screws.

[approach] The usual way in is from Timberline, following the South Side approach, crossing the White River Glacier and continuing around to the foot of the wall, then crossing the bergschrund to reach the start.

name: Newton Clark Headwall
text: [detailed_rack] Bring pickets, an ice axe, crampons and a helmet.
[approach] One option is from Timberline up the White River Glacier;
[approach] the other is directly from the Mt Hood Meadows ski area up the Newton Clark Glacier.
[approach] Bring pickets, ice axe, crampons and a helmet for the glacier approach and the steep headwall above.

name: Wy'East
text: [overview] Start at Timberline Lodge, take the climbers trail to the Palmer lift top, then head east over the glacier called White River;
[overview] roping up is wise among the crevasses.
[overview] The somewhat exposed ridge leads to a snow ramp leaning right, or exposed rock, then a small downclimb, fairly easy if frozen.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, ice axe, an extra tool, crampons and a helmet.
[approach] Head east across the White River Glacier, roped because of crevasses, and climb the moraine to reach the ridge.

name: East Face aka "Brainless Child" (Tyler Adams Memorial Route)
text: [overview] Two snow gully pitches precede the couloir higher up, simul-climbed to the ridge under the summit.
[detailed_rack] Snow pickets, screws, cams.
[approach] The mountain has avalanche, rockfall and icefall hazards, so check the avalanche forecast.

name: Northeast Buttress (McLaughlin Memorial Route)
text: [approach] At its junction with the Pacific Crest Trail, continue straight up the Thielsen Creek drainage toward the remnants of the old glacier.
[approach] The route starts on the east side of the former glacier at the foot of the northeast buttress, with easy slabs below a system of right-facing dihedrals.

name: Western Gulch
text: [detailed_rack] Crampons, tools, slings, one or two pickets, and screws;
[approach] Follow the hiker's route toward the Pacific Crest Trail, or the gully just north of it if snow and conditions favour that.
[approach] At the PCT crossing, look for the west-facing snow apron with avalanche-bent trees;

name: Exegesis
text: [overview] Begin the steep part below the NNE face at a big outcrop right of center, and head straight up between rock towers and snow slopes reaching 70 degrees.
[overview] Prefer snow when it is stable and hides the rock, rock when snow is unstable and the rock bare.
[overview] Move light and fast, as snow softens by mid to late morning;
[detailed_rack] The lower slopes offer many picket placements.

name: March Madness
text: [approach] The base is on the south face of Illumination Rock, below a large hanging snowfield and to the right of the south chamber.
[approach] Higher up, cross the Zigzag Glacier above the Palmer lift;
[approach] it can open crevasses, so rope up after fresh snow.
[descent_text] From the top of the ice you can either climb the steep snowfield to the true summit and rappel the east ridge to the saddle, or rappel the route directly.

name: Skylight
text: [overview] The first wanders over ramps and corners (AI3+ and neve for the party describing it).
[approach] Starting at Illumination Saddle, cross the steep snow under Illumination Rock's north side until you pass a conspicuous rock nose and reach a gentle bowl.
[approach] Illumination Saddle is reached from Timberline Lodge by crossing the Zigzag Glacier above the Palmer lift.

name: Iron Maiden
text: [detailed_rack] Thin conditions call for pins and nuts, while fat ones may allow screws and an occasional picket.

name: Jefferson Park Glacier
text: [overview] The hardest of the glacier lines on this volcano, taken from the north above the meadow basin that serves as the usual base camp.
[overview] Even the easiest side has steep hard snow, so ice tools are expected on this one.

name: Large Ear Direct
text: [overview] scramble along the feature's top to an overhung mantle and a small crevasse you can reach across.

name: North Ridge (Hayden Glacier)
text: [overview] The north ridge, reached from the Pole Creek side and crossing the Hayden glacier.
[detailed_rack] Up to a complete glacier-travel kit, with a fixed line or belayed snow travel depending on the group.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons

name: Southeast Ridge
text: [watch_out] Mid-July snow strip steepens to roughly 40 degrees for a short stretch;
[watch_out] crampons and an axe were used
[descent_text] go back down the snow and scree you came up.
[pro_tips] In mid-July a firm snow strip angling up and right reached the merge of the south and southeast ridges faster than the loose volcanic sand beside it..

name: South Side (Hogsback)
text: [overview] The most-climbed route on Oregon's highest peak, starting from the lodge on its south flank and following the ski area, then a snow ridge between steaming fumaroles, to the summit ridge.
[overview] Most of it is a long snow walk, but the last thousand feet is steep, exposed snow above a bergschrund with rockfall and icefall from the surrounding cliffs.

[beta] From the top of the ski area, climb the snowfield toward the prominent dark buttress of Crater Rock and pass it on its east (climber's right) side, above the sulfur-smelling fumarole area of Devil's Kitchen, to reach the Hogsback, a narrow snow ridge on the no
[beta] Put crampons on at its base.
[beta] The Hogsback ends below a bergschrund that crosses the slope;
[beta] Walk the ridge east to the true summit, staying well back from cornices overhanging the north face.
[hazards] Rockfall and icefall from Crater Rock and the Steel Cliff.
[hazards] Bergschrund below the Hogsback.
[hazards] Long sliding falls on hard or icy snow.
[hazards] Cornices on the summit ridge.
[obj_haz] Snow bridges over the bergschrund and fumaroles weakening through the day.
[obj_haz] Crowds on the steep chutes sending down ice and loose snow
[watch_out] Descending in cloud, the fall line pulls parties toward the Zigzag Glacier and Mississippi Head or into White River Canyon
[watch_out] Keep clear of snowcats and ski traffic in the ski area

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] Suits parties wanting to avoid both the long slog around toward Whitewater Glacier and the intricate North Shoulder finish from Jeff Park Glacier.
[overview] Do it only while snow-covered, because bare it is just scree.
[detailed_rack] Bring picket protection, some screws and maybe a nut or two.
[what_to_bring] two ice tools — especially on the Jeff Park Glacier variation

name: Southwest Ridge
text: [overview] A steep, brushy cross-country climb leads to a scree ridge that joins the South Ridge high on the mountain, then the Red Saddle, a steep snow traverse of about 250 ft, and the summit pinnacle, fourth class or low fifth depending on the line taken.

name: Whitewater Glacier
text: [overview] From a Jefferson Park camp it crosses the moderately crevassed Whitewater Glacier to the southeast ridge, climbs loose scree to the Red Saddle, and crosses a steep snow-and-ice traverse where pickets are usual.
[overview] Rope and glacier gear are standard.
[approach] Leave the trail by the moraine and climb to a bench near 7,100 ft where the glacier starts.
[descent_text] Reverse the route: downclimb or rappel the pinnacle, cross back over the Red Saddle traverse, then descend the scree and the glacier.

name: East Ridge
text: [overview] Plod up the ridge to the last 600ft, a scree (or snow) slope ending at a large, pointed summit.
[approach] The well-worn trail leads to the East Ridge itself, and the final slope to the pointed summit is scree or snow.
[seasonal_guidance] By late October snow can lie on the upper trail, though it stays a trail hike in good weather..
[pro_tips] In early July a snowfield below the summit gave a glissade descent, but it ends well away from the trail;

name: North Milk Creek Glacier
text: [overview] Climbed as a gully, since the glacier has likely melted away.
[overview] Quick going on firm snow, and among the shortest ways up the mountain from the trailhead.

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] a brief crumbly traverse reaches its right side, where gentle snow or cinders finish at the crater edge near the top.

name: Cathedral Ramp
text: [overview] Right: a brief mixed-ice step off the glacier and a long icy traverse merging left.
[overview] Next, cut far left into the snow gully seen from the base;
[overview] P2 (60m): snow, then ice/mixed, then right on loose dry rock exposed to the left, to the top of The Pencil.
[overview] P3 (60m): leftward past the corner across snow and simple rock, aiming for the top of Right Gully.
[overview] P4 (30m): easy snow, crumbly rock.
[overview] Finish with ~500 vertical feet on snow, ice and gentle mixed ground, also used by Ravine, The Pencil and Right Gully.
[approach] The route is on the cleaver's western flank at the head of the Eliot Glacier.
[approach] From the Tilly Jane Hut, follow trails onto the moraine ridge bordering the glacier's east edge, then go up onto the glacier and continue up the upper Eliot Glacier.

name: Cooper Spur
text: [overview] Mount Hood's northeast line, following a long rock spur between the Eliot and Newton Clark glaciers.
[overview] Above it the slope steepens steadily to about 45 degrees and close to 50 near the top, on snow, ice or loose rock, before reaching the summit ridge.
[overview] go early, on firm snow.

name: Eliot Glacier Headwall
text: [detailed_rack] Bring two tools (or a short axe plus a tool), five to eight screws and a couple of pickets.

[approach] From the Cloud Cap and Tilly Jane side, follow the trail past the Tilly Jane cabin to the Cooper Spur trail, then watch for a large cairn marking a use trail that drops to the Eliot Glacier.
[approach] Cross the lower moraine to the west side of the glacier, then work up to the foot of the headwall, crossing crevasses on bridges where you can.

name: North Face Left Gully
text: [overview] Above, the route heads straight to Mt Hood's summit on steep snow with now and then an easy ice step.
[detailed_rack] Screws, pickets, and perhaps a little rock gear.
[approach] Most parties set out at Tilly Jane or Cloud Cap and follow the paths to the moraine ridge bordering the Eliot Glacier's east edge, then cross the glacier to the foot of the North Face.
[approach] The bergschrund is crossed and a belay set below the first pitch of ice.
[descent_text] To return to Tilly Jane, descend Cooper Spur or the Sunshine Route, both on steep snow;
[descent_text] the Sunshine Route has bergschrunds.

name: North Face Right Gully
text: [overview] A cairn on the right marks the way down onto the glacier.
[overview] Keep left on the ice, watching for seracs and crevasses, and angle right near the Eliot headwall.
[overview] The left starts vertical, then is mostly snow.
[detailed_rack] A 60m rope, pickets, and 6-8 short screws.
[approach] Above treeline, climb the lower Cooper Spur ridge until a cairn on the right marks the path down onto the Eliot Glacier.
[approach] Cross the glacier along its left side, watching for seracs and crevasses, and move right as you near the headwall.

name: Ravine
text: [overview] About 50 m of ice makes one full pitch, rising from easy ice through a steep, slightly overhanging bulge (the crux, with poor footholds) to a snow couloir.
[overview] In the couloir, gentler than when viewed from Cathedral ridge, belay off snow pickets.
[detailed_rack] A red BD Camalot in size #1, a Metolius in size #3 (orange), 2-4 pickets, and ice screws (between 5 and 10, by comfort).

[approach] Reach it from the Tilly Jane Hut side by going onto the Eliot Glacier from the lateral moraine, then either traverse toward Cathedral Spire below the Eliot headwall or hike up the glacier past the bergschrund.

name: Sunshine Route
text: [overview] From Cooper Spur the route crosses Eliot Glacier and climbs its right slope toward Horseshoe Rock, easiest to go by on its right.
[overview] Higher up, a bergschrund late in the season can bar the way;
[detailed_rack] Gear typical for glacier travel.
[approach] From the cairn a climbers trail descends onto the Eliot Glacier;
[approach] walk across it toward the Snow Dome, which marks the start of the climbing.

name: East Buttress
text: [overview] The lower part opens with an ice pillar at the toe, probably the crux (snow ramps substitute if it is not formed), then skirts a big buttress on the right, edges left to the crest, scrambles, and follows the narrowing crest across a gendarme to tower number tw

name: KIDS
text: [overview] Past the steep section, a further 20m ramp of AI3 guards the upper snowfield, where the usual headwall line (M3) begins.
[approach] The route is a short ice dagger in the lower right bowl of the Thayer Glacier headwall, on the east side of North Sister.
[approach] Start at the Pole Creek trailhead, leave the trail and head east toward the east side of the mountain to the Thayer Glacier.

name: Thayer Glacier Headwall
text: [approach] Start at the Pole Creek trailhead, leave the trail and head east toward the east side of North Sister, continuing until you reach the Thayer Glacier.
[approach] Once on the glacier, choose one of the gullies;

name: Northwest Ridge
text: [overview] The only way up Broken Top that avoids glacier travel, and the choice for anyone who simply wants the summit.
[descent] the only route with no glacier travel

name: Ramp Route
text: [overview] Snow often lingers late into summer;

name: South Ridge
text: [watch_out] The Terrible Traverse can keep snow patches into mid-August after heavy winters, and the ground under them is loose;
[detailed_rack] Pickets are possible in winter;
[what_to_bring] Ice axe (late July to mid August, for snow on the traverse);
[seasonal_guidance] In late July the traverse toward the Bowling Alley can still be frozen snow at dawn;

name: South Ridge
text: [seasonal_guidance] In late July a long steep snow slope can still fill the Red Saddle traverse, steep enough that a self-arrest is unlikely to hold;
[seasonal_guidance] parties placed pickets or ran a fixed line..

name: Devil's Kitchen Headwall (DKH) - Left Variation
text: [detailed_rack] With fat ice and consolidated snow above, take pickets and medium-length screws.

[approach] The route climbs the long couloir splitting the middle of the Devil's Kitchen Headwall: go up the snow and debris slope below the headwall into the couloir's entrance, then steep snow to the first ice step.

name: Devil's Kitchen Headwall (DKH) - Right Variation
text: [overview] It sits in the corner formed by the headwall and Steel Cliffs, and starts on moderate snow.
[detailed_rack] Kit varies with conditions: 2-3 pickets, ice screws.
[detailed_rack] Early June brought rotten ice-snow on the upper steepening, and firm snow lower, in the runnels.
[approach] The route is tucked into the angle where the headwall above the Devil's Kitchen runs into the Steel Cliffs, and begins on moderate snow.

name: East Crater Wall (DKH V4)
text: [detailed_rack] Pickets hold only where the surface is consolidated, so soloing unprotected may be the sole option.
[approach] Small crevasses can lie at the base.

name: Flying Buttress (DKH V3)
text: [overview] This variant has milder ice than the standard lines and finishes on the upper Wyeast route, with its steep snow crux and exposed gendarme.
[overview] Climb easy ice or moderate snow in the gully toward an apparent dead-end headwall.
[overview] Near its top, go right up an obvious snow ramp to the Wyeast ridge crest, then left along it past a small saddle where DKH V2 joins and a short traverse that may be the crux.
[overview] Moderate to steep, exposed snow follows, easing toward the summit.
[detailed_rack] Bring two tools, or one tool and an axe, plus pickets and a few ice screws if pitching.

name: Icefall Chute (Boy Scouts Chute)
text: [approach] Head uphill, angling slightly right but staying left of the Pearly Gates, and cross the large bergschrund below the chute.
[approach] Icefall is the main worry early in the season and rockfall later.

name: Steel Cliff South Face
text: [overview] Aim for the foot of the first chute, coming from the Palmer snowfield over the glacier and heading toward the Wy'east ridge.
[overview] Climb the snow slope while watching for hazards falling from the cliffs.
[approach] Cross the White River Glacier from the Palmer Snowfield toward the Wy'East ridge to reach the obvious foot of the first chute.

name: West Crater Rim Route (WCR)
text: [overview] Avalanches here have been potentially devastating, one of them deadly: judge the present snow stability, and get across the rim ahead of sunrise heating the slope.

[overview] The route peels off the Pearly Gates/Hogsback line under Crater Rock, bends around the inner side of the western crater edge and traverses sideways up into the Old Chute, away from the crowd on the lower Coleman Glacier.

name: North Face Couloir
text: [overview] Early season, with snow and ice, is best.
[detailed_rack] add screws and pickets for roped climbing.
[approach] The north side has a long approach, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north.
[approach] A bivy on the Skinner Glacier below the face makes it a good two-day trip.

name: North Face of the Northwest Ridge
text: [overview] Early season with abundant snow is best.
[overview] Variation: above the gap, trend up and left to the final rock bands near the crater rim, which can be rotten if snowless;
[detailed_rack] screws and pickets if roped.
[approach] The approach is long, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north.
[approach] Camp on the Skinner Glacier at the foot of the face.

name: Silver Couloir
text: [overview] Takes the leftmost couloir on the north face, climbed straight up from the top of the Skinner Glacier.
[detailed_rack] roped parties add screws and pickets.
[approach] The approach is long, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north;
[approach] Camp on the Skinner Glacier at the foot of the face and treat it as a two-day trip.

name: Prouty Glacier
text: [overview] The glacier is ascended and its headwall passed through a snow chute plus some rock, with rockfall a hazard.
[detailed_rack] Depending on group ability and conditions, a rope and pickets to cross the bergschrund.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe
[approach] From the northern end of the basin, turn uphill by a gully to reach the Prouty Glacier.
[approach] Crampons and an ice axe are needed when there is snow, and a rope and pickets for a possible bergschrund below the rock band.

name: South Side Route
text: [overview] Graded as a scramble (or easy snow), it totals 12.5 miles round trip.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — when snow is present
[approach] It passes the Moraine Lake valley and continues over loose cinder to a sandy saddle at the Lewis Glacier moraine.
[descent_text] The upper trail is loose volcanic scree and cinder that slides underfoot, and with snow cover an ice axe and crampons may be needed.
[seasonal_guidance] In early June the lower trail can still be dusted with fresh snow and the upper slope below the rim is icy enough that crampons and an axe get used..
[pro_tips] The small tarn at the foot of the Lewis Glacier is a spot to refill water in August;

name: Three Sisters Traverse
text: [overview] South and Middle Sister are non-technical scrambles and snow climbs, but North Sister comes last and is the crux: loose Class 3-4 rock, the exposed Terrible Traverse and the rockfall-prone Bowling Alley to its summit pinnacle.

[beta] South Sister (10,358'): from the Devils Lake Trailhead, climb the South Sister climbers' trail through forest and onto the open plateau, then continue north up the South Ridge on steep scree, skirting the Lewis Glacier's moraine lake on its west side, to the c
[beta] Leave the summit down the Northwest Ridge (Class 2, snow early and scree late;
[beta] the Eugene Glacier snowfield lies along its flank) and drop north toward the saddle with Middle Sister above Camp Lake.
[beta] it can hold steep snow or ice early in the season) and follow the upper edge of the Collier Glacier to the saddle between Prouty Point and North Sister.

[beta] Below the summit pinnacle, cross the Terrible Traverse - a steep, exposed snowfield with a nasty runout in early and mid-summer, an easy Class 3 scree crossing once melted out - then turn up into the Bowling Alley, a steep, loose gully between the pinnacle's h
[hazards] Exposed fall on the Terrible Traverse while it holds snow.
[hazards] Steep snow or ice on Middle Sister's North Ridge early in the season.
[hazards] Crevasses where the route skirts the Collier and Hayden glaciers.
[obj_haz] Steep snow with a bad runout.
[watch_out] Cross the Terrible Traverse only when the snow will hold a step - hard ice or afternoon slush both raise the stakes
[watch_out] top up at snowmelt and near Camp Lake
[watch_out] North Sister is reached in the afternoon on this direction - watch the clock and the snow
[gear] Ice axe.

name: Cathedral Ridge
text: [overview] The lower ridge is a tiring slog over scree, and the top part is firm steep snow or more scree.
[detailed_rack] Slings for horns, a pair of pickets and a couple of shorter screws.

name: Leuthold Couloir
text: [approach] Cross the saddle and drop onto the Reid Glacier, then traverse toward Yocum Ridge, going by a number of couloirs on your right, until you reach the steep wall of the ridge.
[approach] starting up too early leads onto the Reid Glacier Headwall instead.
[approach] The slopes are crevassed and avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

name: Reid Glacier Headwall
text: [detailed_rack] Ordinary alpine ice kit otherwise: screws (a handful), pickets (two or three), plus draws in single and double lengths.
[approach] From Timberline Lodge, cross the top of the Zigzag Glacier from the Palmer lift to the saddle between Illumination Rock and the main peak.
[approach] The Reid Glacier lies below to the northwest with Yocum Ridge opposite.

name: Sandy Glacier Headwall
text: [overview] Reached from Illumination Saddle by dropping to the neighbouring glacier and skirting around the foot of Yocum Ridge.
[overview] The route then climbs the glacier named for it and its headwall, where slopes reach about 50 degrees.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, ice axe, an optional ice tool, and the rope, harness and ascenders or prussiks needed for glacier travel.

[approach] Skip Leuthold Couloir and descend close to the ridge to avoid Reid Glacier crevasses, then cross over Yocum Ridge at a low point to the upper Sandy Glacier and traverse to the headwall on its far north side.

name: Yocum Ridge
text: [detailed_rack] Rime makes gear finicky: 4-6 screws, 2-4 pickets, plus a few nuts, some pitons and a few cams, and skill with runouts and improvised anchors.
[approach] Drop from the saddle onto the Reid Glacier and cross it to the start of the ridge.
